note: FNS 1034.2 requires data matching (per Section 512) to verify negative allegations of unemployment compensation — i.e., when a household denies receiving UC. The OLG covers this through the DUA (Department of Unemployment Assistance) match on the PI Checklist, which is listed as a mandatory match that case managers must process. The Matches Overview page states all outstanding matches must be reviewed and appropriate action taken, and BEACON will not allow case authorization when match information has not been dispositioned. The OLG's Unemployment Compensation page provides detailed procedures for processing DUA matches, including scenarios where match data conflicts with client statements. The Simplified Reporting Examples page (Q3/A3) explicitly states the DUA match 'verifies the receipt or non-receipt of Unemployment Compensation,' directly addressing the negative allegation scenario. While the OLG does not use FNS terminology of 'negative allegation,' the functional requirement is fully met: automated data matching identifies cases where clients deny UC but DUA records show otherwise, and workers must act on these matches.
